Resolves #21639

`Neo.gantt.Container#animateCascade` (off by default) moves the tasks a cascade changed from their previous to their final dates over the chart's `--motion-panel` with `--ease-out-soft`, both read from its node. Bars and links read one in-flight span per task (`Container#drawnSpans`), stepped by the new `Neo.gantt.CascadeMotion` on the App Worker, so a link never leaves its bar. The records hold their final dates from the start. The chart reads the tier when the transition is switched on, when it mounts and after each move, so a `0ms` tier (reduced motion), a failed read or one not yet answered leaves the edit's own repaint as the one update. The main thread keeps `Neo.config.prefersReducedMotion` current, so a chart that read a positive tier before the user switched reduced motion on also commits its next edit in one update. A scroll, a zoom, a store load, filter or sort, the next move, and a read that answers no positive tier land a running move at once; binding another store drops it. Both Gantt examples switch it on.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chrome e2e at the head, red on `dev`; unit specs) → L3 required (AC-2, AC-3 and AC-5 are browser observations). Residual: none.

CI jobs: +0 — the e2e spec joins the existing `gantt` selection, the unit spec joins `unit`.

## Deltas from ticket
- **No pre-write hold.** The rows the cascade's writes repaint send their update only after a task boundary (`VdomLifecycle` awaits `timeout(1)` before it collects), so `CascadeMotion#start()` repainting the moved tasks at their previous spans inside the same synchronous edit is what the browser shows first. The e2e's monotonic check would catch a final-then-back flash.
- **A dragged or resized task stays where its preview dropped it,** and its successors travel. Moving it from its old place replayed what the preview had already shown (seen in the first capture). Keyboard, editor and API edits move the edited task too, as the ticket's look says.
- **The tier is read ahead of the moves** (review round 1), as `Neo.app.roundtable.Canvas` reads `--motion-base`: a read answers for the moves after it, so the edit never waits on one and a `0ms`, failed or unanswered read installs no previous span. The easing is read with the duration, so no easing literal sits in JavaScript.
- **Reduced motion reaches a chart that already read a positive tier** (review round 2). `worker/Manager#detectFeatures()` keeps `Neo.config.prefersReducedMotion` current and relays its change to every worker through `setNeoConfig`, the path every runtime config change takes. `CascadeMotion` reads it when a cascade starts and at every step. This is the one engine change outside `src/gantt/`: an App Worker clock cannot read CSS synchronously.
- A running move also lands on a store `sort` or `mutate`, and when the config is switched off. Binding another task store drops it unpainted (review round 1).
- `e2e/gantt/BasicNL.spec.mjs` sets `animateCascade:false`: it measures bars right after moves, and its resize grab missed a still-moving handle.
- `test/playwright/externalBrainSelection.mjs` lists the new spec: like its siblings, it drives the page's own App Worker.

## Addressed Review Feedback (Round 2, review 6000016209)

**RA-2: `[CONTRACT_AMENDED]`.** I took the second route your disposition offers: an explicit contract change by the ticket's design owner. #21639 is mine, and the change leaves #20874's design rule, "Reduced motion means no movement", untouched.

- **Why it can't be discharged in the worker.** An edit must decide at the commit boundary whether to step, using only what the worker knows at that moment. A tier it learns from the read issued at the edit is not known at the commit. The only way to show no intermediate geometry anyway would be to hold the previous spans until the reply, and the RA rules that out as well.
- **Why the trade is safe.** `--motion-panel` is defined once for every theme, in the vocabulary block of `resources/css/src/Global.css`.
